items.title: Using artificial intelligence to mitigate global teacher shortage
items.abstract: Purpose This viewpoint addresses the systemic global teacher crisis – driven by burnout, unsustainable workloads and administrative attrition – and explores the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) tools to reduce non-academic tasks. This piece argues that by using AI to help with administrative burdens, education systems can improve teacher retention, enhance individual student engagement and even support democracy. Design/methodology/approach This piece uses a conceptual and synthesis-based approach, combining a review of current literature with the author's firsthand narrative reflections as a veteran educator and teacher trainer. Findings The piece identifies the root causes of the teacher shortage: the overwhelming volume of non-instructional work. The analysis of the literature supports the use of AI tools to unburden teachers from non-instructional work gaining time to build robust relationships with students, increase the individualization of instruction, all of which can lead to better meeting the learning needs of their students. Finally, it allows for a better life–work balance that can mitigate teacher attrition and attract more quality candidates. Research limitations/implications This is a viewpoint article, and although it is supported by a robust review of relevant literature, it does not put forward new empirical evidence. Practical implications The practical implications of the piece focus on reforming the daily operations of educators' work by integrating AI to eliminate up to six hours of administrative workload per week, thereby reducing teacher burnout and mitigating the global shortage. Social implications The social implications center on safeguarding democratic foundations by stabilizing an endangered education system. Restoring work–life balance through AI helps attract and retain qualified teachers, preventing the systemic collapse of public schooling. Originality/value The originality of this piece is in its unique view of how to mitigate the teacher shortage by embracing AI tools rather than fear them. By using relevant national and international literature in conjunction with the authentic, lived perspective of a veteran educator, the piece provides a fresh approach to combatting the teacher shortage.

items.title: Validating LLM-Generated Expert Judgments in AHP Decision Support: A Preregistered Cross-Study Benchmark and Randomized-Order Audit
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are entering decision-support systems as inexpensive synthetic experts, yet their judgments are rarely validated against published human targets. We benchmark six LLMs on a source-audited corpus of 27 published Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) studies with a preregistered holdout of 22 studies, 21 reference-weight tasks, 28,783 valid benchmark calls, and study-clustered inference. Holdout rank replication was modest and model dependent. A diagnostic showed that fixed-source-order rank evaluation is confounded with criterion presentation order: reference vectors largely follow source listing order, and a model-free descending-order rule reaches a mean Spearman correlation of 0.735, outscoring every model. A prospective randomized-order experiment raised Claude Sonnet 5’s mean Spearman correlation by 0.46, and a registered follow-up with an exactly balanced schedule replicated that gain. For HCX-007, the model that tracks presentation order most strongly, the randomized-order decline was directional but not statistically significant (0.17, Holm p=0.16), and the follow-up was inconclusive about the average difference (+0.007, 95% CI [−0.23, 0.22]); its single draws continued to follow presentation order, and in an exploratory subgroup of six tasks with seven or more criteria its balanced-order accuracy was lower. Most holdout panels could be implemented only as repeated draws under a shared profile, and matched individual human data were limited to two tasks. Benchmarks for synthetic experts should therefore balance presentation order and evaluate aggregate reconstruction, individual human-likeness, and downstream ranking separately.

items.title: Value in app store metadata and user reviews: A dual perspective on quality of Parkinson’s and dementia apps
items.abstract: App stores provide a range of health applications for people living with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). Users like patients can access information from both manufacturer-provided app descriptions and metadata, as well as from user reviews. However, navigating this information to identify value-generating apps of high quality remains challenging. From a health technology assessment (HTA) standpoint, quality is defined by evidence-based medicine, safety, and user-centeredness. To explore the potential value of app store information available to patients, we conducted a descriptive, mixed-methods analysis of unstructured app metadata and user feedback from the Apple App Store and Google Play Store (as of May 2024). We analyzed 1,237 AD/PD-related apps which included 50 duplicates (resulting in 1,187 apps), utilizing descriptive statistics, content analysis, large language model-supported exploratory classification, and a topic modeling approach. In total, only about 2% of the apps claimed to be certified medical devices. Moreover, 24% of Apple apps and 14% of Google apps were in the “Medical” app store genre, among which we found that 63% of Apple and 54% of Google apps were patient-facing. We manually categorized patient-facing apps predominantly under “Care Support,” followed by “Health & Wellness” and “Patient Monitoring.” Importantly, user feedback provided exploratory, potentially valuable patient-reported outcome and experience information but is derived from personal opinions on “user experience,” “health improvement,” and “costs.” As quality information on DHTs could be identified in unstructured app metadata, this information should be improved in trustworthiness and more accessible to users like patients, supporting the public to find high-quality health apps. Furthermore, as user opinions contained information with potential value for patients, these should be explored as complementary value-generating indicators of health apps in future work.

items.abstract: The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for Artificial General Intelligence (ARC-AGI) is a generative, few-shot fluid intelligence benchmark. Although humans effortlessly solve ARC-AGI, it remains extremely difficult for even the most advanced artificial intelligence systems. Inspired by methods for modelling human intelligence spanning neuroscience to psychology, we propose a cognitively inspired ARC-AGI solver. Our solver integrates System 1 intuitions with System 2 reasoning in an efficient and interpretable process using neurosymbolic methods based on Vector Symbolic Algebras (VSAs). Our solver works by object-centric program synthesis, leveraging VSAs to represent abstract objects, guide solution search, and enable sample-efficient neural learning. Preliminary results indicate success, with our solver scoring 10.8% on ARC-AGI-1-Train and 3.0% on ARC-AGI-1-Eval. Additionally, our solver performs well on simpler benchmarks, scoring 94.5% on Sort-of-ARC and 83.1% on 1D-ARC-the latter outperforming GPT-4 at a tiny fraction of the computational cost. Importantly, our approach is unique; we believe we are the first to apply VSAs to ARC-AGI and have developed one of the most cognitively plausible ARC-AGI solvers yet. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ijoffe/ARC-VSA-2025.

items.title: VeriHarness: Scaling Agentic Verification for Long-Horizon Tasks
items.abstract: As LLM agents undertake increasingly complex, long-horizon tasks, verifying their outputs becomes increasingly challenging. We study how verification capability can be strengthened with a fixed base model, without access to reference answers or grading rubrics at test time. Repeated sampling yields multiple rollouts that can contain complementary correct claims, but we need a reliable verification mechanism to determine which claims to trust. We first find that disagreement often exposes correct alternatives, while consensus can conceal errors. These observations motivate VeriHarness, which turns the underlying LLM a generator uses into an agentic verifier by giving it a workspace, evidence tools, and reusable verification skills. A disagreement resolver checks competing claims against environmental evidence, while a consensus challenger tests shared claims and searches for omitted requirements. Their findings guide the selection and revision of the final artifact. Across five long-horizon workspace benchmarks and two frontier models, VeriHarness achieves the highest selection scores among the evaluated baselines. Evidence-backed revision further improves average performance, bringing gains over a single rollout to 6.2 points with Gemini 3.5 Flash and 6.4 points with Claude Opus 4.8. We further show that verification skills can self-improve from failure feedback, demonstrating VeriHarness as a novel and critical approach for scaling long-horizon agentic verification. We release the full pool of approximately 26,000 rollouts across all five benchmarks and both models, produced at a cost of over $100,000, to support future research on agentic verification.

items.title: Virtual Mourning in the Metaverse: User Acceptance, Needs, and Limitations of AI-Based Memory Avatars
items.abstract: Digital transformation is increasingly shaping the ways in which people remember and grieve. While existing platforms and social networks primarily preserve static content, immersive environments such as the metaverse and advances in generative artificial intelligence (AI) enable the creation of interactive, AI-based memory avatars, often also referred to as “griefbots” or “deadbots”. This study examines the perceptions, acceptance, opportunities, as well as psychosocial and ethical limitations of such avatars from the perspective of potential users. To provide an empirical foundation, an interactive prototype was developed and evaluated as part of a quantitative study (N = 33). These results were supplemented by qualitative guided interviews with experts in grief counseling, psychotherapy, and pastoral care. The findings paint a highly ambivalent picture: While respondents see potential in preserving life stories or in processing missed goodbyes, concerns regarding emotional dependence, difficulties in accepting loss, and ethical and data protection risks dominate. The Behavioral Intention to use the technology depends largely on Perceived Usefulness (r = 0.74) and Emotional Impact (r = 0.82), rather than purely on user interface elements. Experts emphasize that simulated interactions must not hinder the necessary process of letting go. The study concludes with recommendations for transparency requirements, time limits, and clear ethical safeguards for vulnerable groups.

items.title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG
items.abstract: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (MRAG) has emerged as a reliable and cost-effective technique of grounding the generative capabilities of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into relevant, up-to-date, external knowledge. Despite presenting several benefits, such as reducing hallucinatory behavior, they also introduce new attack surfaces, including leakage of private information and vulnerabilities against data extraction attacks. In this paper, we introduce $\immrag$, an adaptive and automatic data extraction attack procedure operating in a black box setting against \emph{image-returning} MRAG, a configuration in which the retrieved visual artifact is itself the response. Each query blends an attacker-held shadow image with an image already recovered from the system, and relevance-weighted resampling steers subsequent queries towards regions of the embedding space that still yield novel retrievals. Unlike current extraction attacks that aim to persuade the model towards data leakage by placing a malicious query as a textual prompt, $\immrag$ embeds the malicious instructions inside a user-given input image. We evaluate $\immrag$ on three plausible and distinct real-world scenarios: medical assistant, document-focused helper and general purpose tool. The experiments involve the study of the effectiveness of the attack on multiple CLIP-family retrievers, as well as the impact of various generators. A single 2500-query run reconstructs up to 611 distinct radiology images, 566 document scans and 416 general-purpose images under local-feature correspondence, and reaches up to $5.6\times$ as many distinct datastore items as a non-adaptive baseline. Our results show the urgent need for safeguards specifically designed for multimodal data.

items.title: Wearable-IMU Machine Learning for Exertion and Fatigue Assessment with an Occupational Exoskeleton in Manufacturing
items.abstract: Exoskeletons are increasingly used to reduce physical strain in manual material handling, yet their true influence on worker exertion and fatigue remains challenging to quantify due to the lack of scalable and objective assessment methods. This study introduces a wearable-sensor framework that links subjective workload perception to quantifiable biomechanical responses during realistic industrial tasks, performed with (Exo) and without (NoExo) passive shoulder exoskeleton assistance. Twenty participants completed three representative tasks including loading, overhead screwing, and palletizing, while wearing ten IMUs positioned on the upper trapezius, deltoids, biceps, lumbar erector spinae, and hamstrings. Accelerometer signals (at 148 Hz) were converted to magnitude, segmented into 0.5 s windows with 50% overlap, and reduced to six biomechanical features per sensor, yielding 60 features per window. The dataset comprised 36,901 NoExo and 38,023 Exo windows, each labeled through task-specific Borg-scale mappings. Machine-learning models were evaluated using Leave-One-Participant-Out cross-validation. Random Forest and XGBoost achieved the highest performance (median accuracy = 0.83, F1-weighted = 0.82), outperforming Logistic Regression and Linear Discriminant Analysis. Exoskeleton use decreased inter-participant variability and reduced misclassifications, with top models reaching near-perfect separability for several individuals ( A U C > 0 . 9 5 ). Feature-importance analyses consistently identified the lower back and hamstrings as the most informative sensor locations, enabling up to a 70% reduction in sensor count with minimal performance degradation. Critically, the proportion of hard-exertion windows decreased by nearly 75% with exoskeleton assistance, demonstrating measurable ergonomic benefit. These results establish a deployment-ready approach for real-time, objective assessment of physical workload in manufacturing environments. The proposed framework advances scalable evaluation of assistive technologies, supports data-driven ergonomic design and training, and offers the first evidence that wearable IMU-based machine-learning models can reliably quantify exoskeleton effectiveness in complex, real-world occupational settings.

items.title: Well-being and Buen Vivir: intercultural dialogue between etic and emic perspectives
items.abstract: This study aimed to analyze perceptions of well-being, happiness, and meaning in life among non-indigenous and indigenous participants from the Javaé and Karajá peoples, based on etic and emic perspectives. A qualitative, exploratory, and comparative design was adopted. Participants included 13 indigenous students enrolled in the intercultural education degree program at the Federal University of Goiás and 14 non-indigenous individuals living in the central-west region of Brazil. Data were collected through three open-ended questions addressing well-being, happiness, and meaning in life. Interviews were transcribed verbatim and analyzed using initial and focused coding procedures grounded in constructivist grounded theory, supported by computational tools based on large language models. The findings revealed common categories across both groups, such as family and community relationships, meaningful work and teaching, physical and mental health, and realization of aspirations. However, these categories acquire distinct meanings across different cultural frameworks. Among indigenous participants, well-being was conceived as a relational, collective, and territorially grounded experience, integrating culture, spirituality, ancestry, and nature. In contrast, non-indigenous participants emphasized more individualized narratives, centered on personal progress, consumption, and immediate pleasures. These results highlight the importance of intercultural and decolonial approaches to psychological research on well-being and challenge the universalization of models derived predominantly from WEIRD populations.

items.title: What Can Analogy Tell Us About Artificial Consciousness?
items.abstract: Who or what is conscious? Because subjective experience is directly accessible only in the first person, judgments about consciousness in other entities depend partly on analogy. Historically, such inferences have focused on nonhuman animals, but advances in artificial intelligence have raised the possibility of conscious AI. Here we develop a causal framework for evaluating such evidential analogies. The key distinction is between similarities in factors plausibly involved in generating consciousness and similarities in downstream behavioural or cognitive effects. Our framework weights source-target similarity by causal relevance while allowing for unknown causes, disabling differences and alternative routes to consciousness. Applied to biological systems, it explains why analogical support generally weakens with increasing causal distance from humans. Applied to contemporary AI, it suggests that behavioural similarity provides only limited evidence for consciousness because relevant causal correspondences remain poorly established. The framework also clarifies what evidence would strengthen claims of artificial consciousness.

items.title: Where LLMs Fail with Visualization DSLs
items.abstract: As LLMs take up the role of authoring charts using visualization domain-specific languages (DSLs), the human constraints that shaped those languages may no longer apply, as what is easy for a person is not necessarily easy for a model. To understand how LLMs might work better with DSLs, we explore where and how they fail with current DSL designs. We evaluate 10 JSON-style visualization DSLs with 41 tasks across 3 LLMs, then assess the generated specifications with JSON and rendering checks, and qualitative coding of failed cases. Analyzing how this specification generation process fails, we identify four recurring failure patterns, link each to specific DSL features, and discuss design considerations for future DSL designs.

items.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
items.abstract: On-policy self-distillation has recently emerged as an effective approach for improving language-model reasoning by supervising students with a frozen or EMA version of themselves that receives privileged information. Its application to multimodal large language models (MLLMs), however, remains largely unexplored. Recent approaches use privileged visual information, such as image crops corresponding to a question, to improve fine-grained perception, but their gains are confined to tasks that benefit from such visual zooming and require either human-annotated grounding data or external teacher models. We introduce a different form of on-policy self-distillation for MLLMs that provides the teacher with textual, spatially grounded guidance identifying the visual elements relevant to a query. We use procedurally generated scenes with automatically available object identities and spatial coordinates, enabling scalable and annotation-free post-training. The teacher uses this spatial guidance to locate and integrate evidence from multiple relevant image regions, while the student learns to reproduce the resulting behavior from the image and question alone. Our approach consistently improves performance on counting, document and chart understanding benchmarks across multiple models. Importantly, although post-training uses only synthetic scenes, the resulting improvements transfer to real-world perception benchmarks, yielding a 3.23-point gain in average performance across CVBench, V*, ZoomBench, BLINK, HR-Bench, and MME-RealWorld. These results show that spatially grounded privileged information can induce broader perceptual capabilities through on-policy self-distillation, enabling substantial synthetic-to-real transfer beyond the task and data distribution used for post-training. items.title: Which Evaluation Strategies Help Students Spot Visual Misinformation on Social Media?
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Background The rapid spread of visual misinformation online, intensified by advances in generative artificial intelligence, presents new challenges for adolescents' digital information literacy. Although students' difficulties in evaluating online information are well documented, little is known about how they assess different forms of visual misinformation on social media. Objectives This study examined the extent to which lower secondary school students can successfully identify different types of visual misinformation on social media, the evaluation strategies they use, and whether these strategies predict misinformation detection across types of visual misinformation. Methods The participants were 272 students in Grades 7–9 who evaluated social media posts containing visual misinformation, including manipulated videos, manipulated images, and AI‐generated images. Students rated each item's credibility and provided written justifications. Evaluation strategies were coded using a theoretically grounded scheme. Results Students were moderately successful in identifying manipulated images and videos, but struggled to detect AI‐generated images, which were often perceived as credible. Students relied primarily on evaluation of visual appearance and content, while source evaluation and corroboration strategies were infrequently used. Across all visual misinformation types, examination of visual features, knowledge‐based evaluation, sourcing, and corroboration strategies predicted misinformation detection. However, corroboration was the only strategy that reliably predicted identification of AI‐generated images. Conclusions Students mostly rely on first‐hand evaluation of visual appearance and content, but these strategies are inadequate for detecting realistic AI‐generated visual misinformation. Instruction should emphasize active verification strategies, particularly corroboration, and support students in coordinating multiple evaluation strategies when engaging with online visual information.

items.title: Who Thinks First? Designing Productive Friction with Engage-to-Unlock GenAI
items.abstract: Generative AI can support writing, but frictionless access may cause cognitive offloading before users develop their own ideas. We introduce Engage-to-Unlock, a productive-friction mechanism that unlocks generative capabilities after users meaningfully engage with the task. In a controlled experiment (N = 398), participants completed a writing task under one of four conditions: Human-Only, Standard Chatbot, Engage-to-Unlock, or Time-Matched Unlock, which matched unlock timing to Engage-to-Unlock participants but independent of users' engagement, then evaluated passages for evidence and inferential errors. Results show that Engage-to-Unlock redistributed effort across tasks: participants spent more time writing and less time evaluating, without increasing overall task duration. They also submitted more prompts than in other AI-assisted conditions and showed the highest accuracy-per-time evaluation efficiency across conditions. These findings suggest that designing GenAI access to encourage early human engagement may provide a productive form of friction, while retaining active AI use and efficient downstream evaluation.

items.title: WHY PYTHON PROGRAMMING IN PHARMACEUTICAL SCIENCE?
items.abstract: The rapid digital transformation of the pharmaceutical sector has created a growing demand for professionals who can combine pharmaceutical knowledge with computational and data-analytic skills. Python programming has emerged as a valuable educational and professional tool because of its simple syntax, open-source nature, extensive scientific libraries, and applicability in data analysis, visualization, automation, pharmacokinetics, pharmacovigilance, formulation research, clinical studies, bioinformatics, quality control, and artificial intelligence-assisted drug development. The revised B.Pharm curriculum introduced by the Pharmacy Council of India under the NEP 2020 framework recognizes this changing professional environment by including Basics of Python Programming for Pharmaceutical Sciences at the undergraduate level. This curricular development represents an important shift from conventional computer literacy toward structured programming, pharmaceutical data handling, scientific visualization, and computational problem-solving. The present review examines the rationale for incorporating Python programming into pharmaceutical education and correlates the revised curriculum with emerging requirements of the pharmaceutical industry. Particular emphasis is placed on the relevance of NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, data cleaning, CSV/Excel processing, pharmacokinetic datasets, adverse drug reaction analysis, dissolution-profile visualization, research data management, and introductory pathways toward machine learning and artificial intelligence. The review further discusses the potential contribution of Python competency to pharmaceutical research and development, quality assurance, manufacturing, regulatory science, clinical research, pharmacovigilance, and Pharma 4.0. Challenges related to faculty training, infrastructure, limited instructional hours, data integrity, validation, and responsible use of artificial intelligence are also considered. It is concluded that Python should not be regarded merely as an additional programming subject in the pharmacy curriculum, but as a foundational digital competency capable of improving data literacy, research capability, interdisciplinary collaboration, and industrial readiness among future pharmacy graduates. This article cover subject wisr role of python programming in pharmaceutical industries.

items.title: Wildlife Monitoring System Using GSM System
items.abstract: The increasing incidence of wild animal intrusion in agricultural areas poses significant risks to both human safety and crop productivity. This project, AI-IoT Smart Animal Surveillance for Human Safety, proposes a real-time monitoring system that integrates Artificial Intelligence (AI) with Internet of Things (IoT) to detect, alert, and assess the presence of wild animals near farms. The system utilises a Raspberry Pi equipped with a camera module and employs the YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) object detection algorithm to accurately identify animals from live video feeds. Upon detection, the system captures the image, sends an email alert with timestamp and location to the farmer, and activates a buzzer to warn nearby individuals. Additionally, IoT-based health monitoring sensors such as temperature, heartbeat, and gas sensors are used to evaluate the physical condition and surrounding environment of the detected animals, aiding early detection of diseases or environmental threats. The system operates in real-time and ensures quick response to critical situations, thereby minimizing crop damage and reducing the risk of human-animal conflicts. It is designed to be cost-effective, energy-efficient, and easy to deploy in rural and remote areas. Furthermore, the system can be enhanced with features such as mobile application integration, cloud-based data storage, and GPS tracking for better monitoring and control. Overall, the proposed system provides a smart, automated, and reliable solution for wildlife surveillance and safety management.

items.title: WIP: DBWorkout: A Gamified SQL Practice Platform to Support Formative Learning in Database Courses
items.abstract: This research WIP paper presents DBWorkout, a web-based platform that supports formative SQL learning through sandbox-based execution, automated result-based feedback, and session-based gamification. Learning Structured Query Language (SQL) remains challenging for undergraduate students due to limited opportunities for interactive practice and immediate feedback. Students iteratively practice SQL on live database instances while receiving multi-dimensional feedback on query correctness, including row values, column structure, and ordering. To reduce instructor workload, DBWorkout incorporates large language model (LLM)-assisted tools for schema and task generation within a human-in-the-loop workflow. A pilot study with teaching assistants and a classroom deployment involving 170 undergraduate students across two in-class sessions show strong perceived learning value (90% agreement) and engagement (87% enjoyment), alongside low reported pressure (22%). However, only 42% of students found the automated feedback sufficiently actionable, a finding independently corroborated by 40% of open-ended responses raising feedback quality concerns, providing cross-method triangulation of this gap. These findings demonstrate the technical feasibility and early pedagogical potential of DBWorkout while identifying directions for enhancing feedback quality and supporting sustained SQL learning.

items.title: WISDOM THAT GUIDES A CHILD'S HEART TO HAPPINESS
items.abstract: This article examines the role and pedagogical potential of aphorisms and words of wisdom in the spiritual and moral upbringing of a child. Concise yet profoundly meaningful aphorisms exert a powerful influence on instilling virtues such as goodness, kindness, patience, gratitude, humility, honesty, the pursuit of knowledge, and self-awareness in a child's heart. The paper conducts a pedagogical analysis of selected aphorisms from Anvar Ahmad’s work “Encyclopedia of Wisdom: Aphorisms Leading to Happiness.” Particular emphasis is placed on the psychological impact of these aphorisms on primary school pupils, their practical integration into daily life, and opportunities for collaborative application within the student–teacher–parent paradigm. Wisdom is interpreted not as ready-made didactic preaching, but as a spiritual tool that cultivates critical thinking, situational awareness, and constructive independent reflection.

items.title: Workforce Challenges and Operational Realities in the Era of Extreme Wildfire
items.abstract: This chapter examines the rapidly changing realities confronting the wildland firefighting workforce as climate change produces longer fire seasons, larger and more extreme wildfires, and increasingly complex operational demands. It considers how repeated exposure to intense heat, hazardous smoke, difficult terrain, long deployments, and unpredictable fire behavior affects the people responsible for protecting communities, ecosystems, and critical infrastructure. These environmental and operational pressures intersect with persistent workforce challenges, including difficulties in recruitment and retention, uneven access to training, staffing shortages, inadequate compensation, limited career pathways, and inconsistent institutional support.Drawing on research in wildland fire operations, human performance, occupational health, and workforce management, the chapter assesses the cumulative effects of these conditions on firefighters’ physical safety, mental health, job performance, family lives, and long-term career decisions. Particular attention is given to fatigue, injury, respiratory and cardiovascular risks, trauma, burnout, and the organizational cultures that may discourage personnel from seeking help. The discussion also considers how temporary employment structures, geographic disparities, and barriers affecting underrepresented groups can undermine workforce resilience and institutional knowledge.The chapter concludes by identifying evidence-based strategies for building a safer, stronger, and more sustainable workforce. These include competitive pay and benefits, clearer professional standards, expanded training and leadership development, improved health monitoring, accessible mental health services, predictable scheduling, and stronger pathways to permanent employment. It also highlights policy reforms needed to modernize workforce systems, strengthen accountability, and ensure that wildland firefighters receive resources and recognition commensurate with roles that are becoming more critical—and more demanding—each passing year.

items.title: Workplace health investment and employment adjustment public health evidence from CSR reports of Chinese A-share listed firms
items.abstract: This study examines whether workplace-health-related corporate practices disclosed in corporate social responsibility (CSR) reports are associated with firm-level employment adjustment. Using 12,669 firm-year observations of Chinese A-share non-financial listed firms from 2013 to 2024, we construct a sentence-level measure of CSR-disclosed workplace health practice intensity and relate it to employment growth and residual employment-adjustment volatility. The indicator captures the relative intensity of disclosed occupational health and safety, medical support, mental-health services, health promotion and working-condition improvements. In firm and year fixed-effects models, a one-standard-deviation increase in disclosure intensity is associated with approximately 2.4% points higher employment growth and 0.012 higher three-year adjustment volatility. The associations are accompanied by lower disclosed work-injury rates and employee turnover, and the volatility pattern is concentrated in positive residual adjustment and industry upturns. Instrumental-variable and sample-selection analyses yield estimates consistent with the baseline fixed-effects results and the proposed occupational-health service channel. The results support an interpretation of lower occupational-health-related labor frictions and stronger expansion-oriented employment responsiveness. The study contributes evidence on the labor-market implications of corporate resource allocation toward workplace health governance and provides a firm-level basis for further health-economic evaluation.

items.title: Workplace responses to perpetration of family and domestic violence: a global scoping review
items.abstract: Introduction Family and domestic violence (FDV), which includes intimate partner and family violence, affects workplace safety through spillover impacts on workers, organisations, and occupational health systems. To date, workplace interventions addressing the issue of FDV have predominantly concentrated on providing support to victim-survivors, while there is limited research regarding employer responses to employees who perpetrate such violence. Method A scoping review was conducted following Arksey and O’Malley’s framework and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines, which examined existing evidence from workplace policies, practices, and organisational mechanisms addressing FDV perpetration by workers. Peer-reviewed studies and high-quality grey literature on workplace responses to perpetration of FDV were systematically searched across multiple databases and online sources, and 28 documents on workplace responses to FDV perpetration were analysed. Results Findings from the scoping review reveal four dominant insights across the literature: 1. Perpetration of FDV is a major workplace problem, yet responses are under-researched; 2. Workplaces employ wide-ranging and varied responses, from zero tolerance dismissal of perpetrators to responsibility avoidance; 3. Responses lack a solid evidence-base and regulatory frameworks to address the problem remain weak; 4. Practical strategies are provided to better manage risk, strengthen safety, and reduce violence. Conclusion Our findings underscore the need for clearer organisational guidance, evidence-based strategies, and robust regulatory frameworks to strengthen workplace responses to FDV perpetration and improve occupational safety outcomes. Practical applications Effective workplace responses to perpetration of FDV should consider work design factors, referral pathways and confidentiality protections which are guided by graduated accountability models and regulatory frameworks.

items.title: Zenodo Metadata — Be: Founding Business Proposal v2.0
items.abstract: Be is a proposed organization dedicated to making safe, professionally governed artificial intelligence emotional support freely accessible to people who need someone to talk to. Be proposes an AI emotional-support system designed around a foundational distinction: an AI must never confuse what it observes with what it infers. Version 2.0 further develops the proposal's framework for adaptive conversational communication through the principle Adaptive Tone, Fixed Boundaries. Be may adapt its tone, vocabulary, pacing, humor, warmth, and conversational style to meet an individual where they are, while maintaining fixed ethical and relational boundaries. The system should allow human-like communication without creating a false human identity, adapting the interface without fabricating the relationship. The proposal incorporates Red Tape Theory™ as a proposed safety methodology: Observe. Record. Question. Do not force the axiom. Interpretation must never be represented as observation. Be does not propose to diagnose users or replace licensed mental-health professionals. Instead, it proposes a professionally governed pathway through which an AI system may recognize when AI-only support may no longer be an appropriate level of support and facilitate access to human care. A proposed charitable human-care program, If You Get It, You Get It, would seek to use charitable resources to help people access licensed professional care when professionally established safety criteria indicate that additional human support may be appropriate. Version 2.0 expands the proposal's treatment of personalization as a safety boundary, including the distinction between adapting communication to an individual and constructing a misleading simulated relationship. It also addresses clinical governance, privacy, autonomy, human handoff, crisis safety, documentation, intellectual-property considerations, research and evaluation, and a potential future child-focused system provisionally called NewBee. This publication is a founding proposal and does not represent a deployed clinical service, licensed mental-health treatment program, clinical efficacy claim, professional endorsement, or completed charitable program. Be begins with the question: Where could this harm somebody?

items.title: Как могат да се ускорят бавните структури? Институционална инфраструктура за организационния капитал на малкия и средния бизнес
items.abstract: Работната бележка продължава „Защо пирамидата на доходите в България е толкова стръмна“ и „Бързи институции, бавни структури“. Те стигат до извод в три стъпки: изоставането в производителността е вътре в отраслите и е най-голямо при местните фирми; при нововъведенията то е най-голямо в организацията на работата, а не в продуктите; вероятна причина е прекъснатият частен организационен капитал. Самото управление обаче не е измерено пряко. Бележката пита дали публичните институции могат да намалят времето и цената за придобиване на организационен капитал, без да заместват пазарния подбор. Предлага „институционална инфраструктура за организационен капитал“: доброволна диагностика, стандартни управленски инструменти, практическо консултиране, по-малка административна тежест за участниците и помощ при преструктуриране, продажба или прекратяване на фирмата. Показва, че процедурата по стабилизация в Търговския закон съществува от 2017 г., но между 2017 и 2022 г. е използвана само 12 пъти. Два полеви експеримента подкрепят управленското консултиране, но ефектите силно се различават между програмите. Затова бележката не предлага национална програма, а три пилота с предварително заявени критерии за оценка и прекратяване. Подготвена с помощта на ChatGPT (OpenAI) и Claude (Anthropic); числата са сверени с посочените източници. Пълен текст на български. This working note follows two earlier notes on Bulgaria's income distribution and on the historical layers of its economy. They reach a three-step conclusion: the productivity gap lies within sectors and is largest among domestically controlled firms; in innovation, the gap is widest in the organisation of work rather than in products; a likely cause is the interrupted stock of private organisational capital, although management itself has not been measured directly. The note asks whether public institutions can reduce the time and cost of acquiring organisational capital without replacing market selection. It proposes an "institutional infrastructure for organisational capital": voluntary firm diagnostics, standard management tools, practical consulting, lower administrative burden for participants, and help with restructuring, transfer or exit. It shows that Bulgaria's pre-insolvency stabilisation procedure has existed since 2017 but was used only 12 times between 2017 and 2022. Two field experiments support management consulting, but effects vary widely across programmes. The note therefore proposes three pilots with pre-registered evaluation and termination criteria rather than a national programme. Prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic). Full text in Bulgarian.

items.title: Как могат да се ускорят бавните структури? Институционална инфраструктура за организационния капитал на малкия и средния бизнес
items.abstract: Работната бележка продължава „Защо пирамидата на доходите в България е толкова стръмна“ и „Бързи институции, бавни структури“. Те стигат до извод в три стъпки: изоставането в производителността е вътре в отраслите и е най-голямо при местните фирми; при нововъведенията то е най-голямо в организацията на работата, а не в продуктите; вероятна причина е прекъснатият частен организационен капитал. Самото управление обаче не е измерено пряко. Бележката пита дали публичните институции могат да намалят времето и цената за придобиване на организационен капитал, без да заместват пазарния подбор. Предлага „институционална инфраструктура за организационен капитал“: доброволна диагностика, стандартни управленски инструменти, практическо консултиране, по-малка административна тежест за участниците и помощ при преструктуриране, продажба или прекратяване на фирмата. Показва, че процедурата по стабилизация в Търговския закон съществува от 2017 г., но между 2017 и 2022 г. е използвана само 12 пъти. Два полеви експеримента подкрепят управленското консултиране, но ефектите силно се различават между програмите. Затова бележката не предлага национална програма, а три пилота с предварително заявени критерии за оценка и прекратяване. Подготвена с помощта на ChatGPT (OpenAI) и Claude (Anthropic); числата са сверени с посочените източници. Пълен текст на български. This working note follows two earlier notes on Bulgaria's income distribution and on the historical layers of its economy. They reach a three-step conclusion: the productivity gap lies within sectors and is largest among domestically controlled firms; in innovation, the gap is widest in the organisation of work rather than in products; a likely cause is the interrupted stock of private organisational capital, although management itself has not been measured directly. The note asks whether public institutions can reduce the time and cost of acquiring organisational capital without replacing market selection. It proposes an "institutional infrastructure for organisational capital": voluntary firm diagnostics, standard management tools, practical consulting, lower administrative burden for participants, and help with restructuring, transfer or exit. It shows that Bulgaria's pre-insolvency stabilisation procedure has existed since 2017 but was used only 12 times between 2017 and 2022. Two field experiments support management consulting, but effects vary widely across programmes. The note therefore proposes three pilots with pre-registered evaluation and termination criteria rather than a national programme. Prepared with the assistance of ChatGPT (OpenAI) and Claude (Anthropic). Full text in Bulgarian.

items.abstract: Abstract The rapid development of digital technologies has transformed modern society in almost every sphere of human life. The growth of the internet, smartphones, social media, artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data, digital payments, e-commerce, and online education has created what is commonly described as a digital society. Digital technologies have improved communication, access to information, education, healthcare, business, public administration, and economic participation. At the same time, the increasing dependence on digital systems has created significant ethical challenges relating to privacy, data protection, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, misinformation, digital inequality, online harassment, intellectual property, surveillance, and the responsible use of emerging technologies.

items.title: A brief study of Tribal Brick Workers: Special reference of Thane district
items.abstract: Abstract- Brick’s manufacturing is an important industry in India. Bricks are very important raw material required in construction. Thousands of construction projects are ongoing in Mumbai Economic zone and thane district. Bricks manufacturers in thane district are primary suppliers of bricks to these construction sites. Large number of tribal communities from thane district are engaged as bricks worker in Bricks manufacturing Industry. These Tribal Brick workers play an important role in the construction industry, providing the foundation for buildings, homes, and other infrastructure projects. Despite their significant contribution, they have very challenging lives. Harsh physical labour, prolong working hours, and limited resources is an everyday issue for these workers. These tribal workers have lack of formal education, which limits their employment opportunities outside the brick industry. These workers Often employed on a seasonal basis, with very low wages, long working hours, and. Due to illiteracy and poor economic condition times, they often exploited by their owners. This article will focus on the working and living conditions of brick workers in the Thane district. This research aims to understand the socio-economic status and problems, occupational health issues, and the impact of their work environment on their overall well-being of Tribal Bricks Wokers. This paper is going to focus on the problems and possible remedies to address the various issues of Tribal Brick Workers. This research will be helpful to the broader discourse on informal labours problems and provides a foundation for policymakers and social organizations to address the challenges faced by brick workers.

items.title: A Fatigue-Gated Hold on Outbound Messages: A Technical Note for Communication-Platform-as-a-Service (CPaaS) Systems
items.abstract: When a person approves an action while tired, the AI agent that carries it out may send a message that cannot be taken back, a refund, an alert, an account change. This note suggests a simple fix: before sending, check if the approving person showed signs of fatigue. If so, hold the message briefly for a second look before it goes out. This applies to any communication platform that sends such messages on behalf of a human or an AI agent, including Zoho CPaaS, Twilio, and Infobip.

items.title: A federated explainable artificial intelligence architecture for multimodal disaster intelligence and response coordination
items.abstract: Natural disasters demand rapid synthesis of fragmented, heterogeneous data often distributed across independently governed organizations. This paper introduces DisasterAI, a federated, cloud-native, and multi-modal AI architecture for disaster intelligence. Unlike centralized analytics platforms, DisasterAI emphasizes federated data ingestion, modular adapters, and the alignment of derived intelligence—enabling cross-agency coordination without requiring raw data consolidation. The architecture integrates satellite imagery (optical and SAR), IoT sensor streams, public alerts, and contextual civic data into a unified, explainable decision-support pipeline. DisasterAI addresses critical challenges in disaster intelligence, including spatial-temporal alignment of asynchronous data, modality-aware fusion, uncertainty representation, and fairness-aware decision-making. Designed to support the entire disaster lifecycle—from early warning and forecast-informed risk analysis to impact assessment and response prioritization—it operates within a human-in-the-loop decision-support context. A scenario-driven evaluation illustrates how DisasterAI enhances coordination effectiveness, improves prioritization consistency, and maintains robustness under partial data availability. By focusing on architectural behavior and operational integration rather than algorithmic benchmarking, this work positions federated, explainable AI systems as a viable foundation for scalable and reliable disaster-response frameworks in complex, data-constrained environments.

items.title: A Feminist Stylistic study of AI-Generated and Human-Written Short Stores: A Comparative Study
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI raises serious questions about potential differences in story construction between human and AI narratives, particularly in terms of cultural and social artifacts. The research addresses the gap in feminist stylistic studies on AI-generated fiction by conducting a comparative analysis of feminist representations in AI-generated and human-written fiction. By analyzing these narratives, the current research sheds light on the extent to which AI-generated short stories stylistically compare to human-written short stories in terms of feminism. The research is guided by two questions: How do the linguistic choices used in AI-generated and human-written short stories, when analyzed through a feminist lens, reflect or challenge patriarchal thinking? And what are the main similarities and differences between AI-generated and human-written short stories in respect to feminist portrayal? The analysis employs Mills' (1995) feminist stylistic model, with emphasis on endearment terms, metaphor, transitivity, fragmentation, and focalization. The research examines one human-written short story titled Dinner Conversation (2020) and one AI-generated short story titled The Crack in the Bowl (2026) using a carefully standardized prompting process. The findings indicate that both stories perpetuate traditional gender hierarchies, albeit through diverse linguistic mechanisms. According to the research, AI, specifically ChatGPT-5.2, is more progressive in terms of gendered assumptions than the human author. In human-written stories, patriarchy is more pervasive and stable, whereas in AI-generated stories, it is more nuanced and sometimes contradictory. This research adds to the emerging studies on AI storytelling by demonstrating how AI-generated fiction can both duplicate and disrupt traditional gender stereotypes.

items.title: A framework for institutional change in the age of AI
items.abstract: Generative AI is rapidly reshaping STEM higher education. Not only are our educational practices changing, but how we think about educational transformation must also adapt. Existing models of institutional change in STEM, aimed at interactive engagement, have largely followed an adoption logic: relatively stable, well-researched educational practices are evaluated and then scaled. These assumptions do not hold for generative AI, which is an arrival technology – entering classrooms before a sufficient pedagogical evidence base could form, and requiring institutions to act under uncertainty. Building on recent decades of work on STEM education institutional change, we propose a framework identifying six dimensions along which prior models of change must be adapted in light of AI: three concerning the tools at the center of reform (the tool’s evidence base, rate of change, and scope), and three concerning the people involved in change (faculty, change agents, and students). For each dimension, we examine how AI-era assumptions differ from those underlying prior STEM education reforms and derive design implications, including: privileging humble and local inquiries; organizing reform around pedagogical approaches rather than specific tools; repositioning change agents as facilitators of collective inquiry; and engaging students as partners in reform. Collectively, the six dimensions and design implications constitute a framework for adapting change models to support institutions under conditions of genuine uncertainty. Finally, we illustrate how the framework may be applied through a brief case-study of a faculty workshop series carried out in a university physics department to support instructors adapting to this modern AI era.

items.title: A Generative AI Framework to Predict Cardiomyocyte Contraction Function From Single Static Images
items.abstract: Understanding how cardiomyocyte structure governs contractile function is fundamental to cardiac biology and disease modeling, yet current approaches rely on time‐resolved imaging and computationally intensive analysis. Here, we present a generative artificial intelligence (AI) framework that directly predicts contractile behavior of human‐induced pluripotent stem cell‐derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC‐CMs) from single static images. Our approach integrates a U‐Net‐based generator with a patch‐based generative adversarial network (GAN) discriminator to translate morphological and sarcomere structural features into pixel‐resolved contraction heatmaps. To further enhance performance and generalizability, we incorporated synthetic cell–function pairs generated via a StyleGAN2 framework, improving prediction accuracy and perceptual similarity. Region‐specific and whole‐cell analyses revealed that AI predictions capture biologically meaningful structure–function relationships, with sarcomere organization strongly associated with both contractile output and prediction fidelity. Reconstruction error emerged as an interpretable metric reflecting localized inefficiencies in sarcomere‐to‐contraction coupling. Together, this framework establishes a scalable, interpretable strategy for inferring cardiomyocyte function from static morphology, eliminating the need for time‐lapse imaging, and positions generative AI as a powerful tool for bridging cellular structure and function to advance high‐throughput phenotyping and in vitro cardiac modeling.

items.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
items.abstract: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. items.title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
items.abstract: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.
